item.content:encoded:
This is a fun SCP, +1. If this SCP were relocated to the southern hemisphere, would the death/ animation cycle reverse (i.e., dead from March-September)?

Also, a little nitpick: I find it odd that an SCP that draws its inspiration from a Greek myth would adhere to our current, Gregorian calendar. I suggest replacing the "March 21" and "September 21" to the "Spring Equinox" and the "Autumn Equinox", respectively.

I know this SCP is a Series I and 8+ years old and unlikely to change.

item.content:encoded:
Made a grammatical edit to change "to avoid take risks" to "to avoid taking risks."
I feel like other grammar could be tightened up, but I'm not sure how much editing I can do while remaining "minor."
In particular, "subjects will take extreme lengths" doesn't sound very natural to me. Would prefer "subjects will go to extreme lengths" or rewrite the sentence entirely as "Furthermore, subjects will demonstrate extreme aversion to any sort of risk or danger to their person, even if they had displayed risk-taking behaviors prior to ingesting SCP-156."

Subjects that undergo a single death-reanimation cycle display irrational fear towards their temporary deaths,

How does the foundation know that the fear is irrational? They can't explain their fear, but it might be because of knowledge they can't consciously access, knowledge which would make the fear entirely rational.

item.content:encoded:
I don't quite understand the 910 conflict. Would the 156-affected not die annually with 910, or at least think so, and try to break out until death? Would they not be able to die otherwise and continue the resurrection cycle indefinitely? The former case only deserves to be a non-bolded footnote or some such, as subjects aren't normally made privy to other SCPs anyway, and exposure isn't a big deal. I assume the latter is not much of a problem either, as 910 victims can still be killed with total body destruction.

So, what's the deal?
